questions.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^{2}$ over $0\le x\le2$ using $2$ equal strips and midpoint heights.

options.why: Used the left endpoints $0$ and $1$ instead of the midpoints, giving $(0^{2}+1^{2})(1)=1$.
Used the right endpoints $1$ and $2$ instead of the midpoints, giving $(1^{2}+2^{2})(1)=5$.
Added the midpoint values without squaring them, giving $(0.5+1.5)(1)=2$.

questions.solution_text:
$\Delta x=\frac22=1$, and the midpoints are $0.5$ and $1.5$.
The sum is $[(0.5)^{2}+(1.5)^{2}](1)=2.5$.

questions.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^{2}$ over $0\le x\le1$ using $2$ equal strips and midpoint heights.

options.why: Added the rectangle heights but omitted multiplication by the strip width $0.5$.
Used the left endpoints $0$ and $0.5$, giving $(0^{2}+0.5^{2})(0.5)=0.125$.
Used the midpoint values as heights without squaring them, giving $(0.25+0.75)(0.5)=0.5$.

questions.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^{2}$ over $1\le x\le3$ using $2$ equal strips and midpoint heights.

options.why: Used the left endpoints $1$ and $2$, giving $(1^{2}+2^{2})(1)=5$.
Used the right endpoints $2$ and $3$, giving $(2^{2}+3^{2})(1)=13$.
Did not square the midpoint values, giving $(1.5+2.5)(1)=4$.

questions.question_text: Find the value of $\lim_{\Delta x\to0}\sum_{3}^{8}(2x+5)\,\Delta x$.

options.why: Found the average endpoint height $\frac{11+21}{2}=16$ but omitted multiplication by the interval width $5$.
Used the left endpoint height $11$ for the whole interval, giving $11(5)=55$ instead of the limiting area.
Used the right endpoint height $21$ for the whole interval, giving $21(5)=105$ instead of the limiting area.

questions.solution_text:
The limit is the area under $y=2x+5$ from $x=3$ to $x=8$.
The endpoint heights are $11$ and $21$.
The trapezium area is $\frac{8-3}{2}(11+21)=80$.

questions.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^{2}$ over $0\le x\le3$ using $3$ equal strips and midpoint heights.

options.why: Used left endpoint heights, giving $(0^{2}+1^{2}+2^{2})(1)=5$.
Used right endpoint heights, giving $(1^{2}+2^{2}+3^{2})(1)=14$.
Did not square the midpoint values, giving $(0.5+1.5+2.5)(1)=4.5$.

questions.solution_text:
Each strip has width $1$, with midpoints $0.5$, $1.5$ and $2.5$.
The sum is $0.25+2.25+6.25=8.75$.

questions.question_text: A car has positive velocity throughout $0\le t\le6$ seconds. Estimate its travel using $3$ equal time strips and midpoint rectangles. Its velocities at $t=1$, $3$ and $5$ seconds are $5$, $9$ and $14$ m/s respectively.

options.why: Added the velocities but omitted multiplication by the time-strip width $2$ seconds.
Multiplied the sum of the velocities by the whole interval length $6$ instead of each strip's width $2$.
Used the last supplied velocity $14$ m/s throughout all $6$ seconds, giving $14(6)=84$ m.

questions.question_text: Calculate the Riemann sum for $f(x)=x^{2}$ over $1\le x\le3$ using $4$ equal strips and midpoint heights.

options.why: Added the midpoint heights but omitted multiplication by the strip width $0.5$.
Used left endpoint heights, giving $(1^{2}+1.5^{2}+2^{2}+2.5^{2})(0.5)=6.75$.
Used right endpoint heights, giving $(1.5^{2}+2^{2}+2.5^{2}+3^{2})(0.5)=10.75$.
